name: FDE 企业 AI 交付进阶训练班
description: 面向已有 AI Engineering 能力的在职工程师，用多个客户案例训练企业 AI 方案、实现、评估与交付。
description_en: Advanced enterprise AI delivery practice for engineers who can already build and debug AI applications.
targetAudience: 已有 AI Engineering 能力，希望承担企业客户项目的在职工程师。
timeLength: 10 周；每周 3 小时工作坊，课外约 3–5 小时
cardDescription: FDE Tech：10 周、30 项工程交付任务。从客户调查与预算到企业系统接入、Evals、客户 Pre 和运行交接。

prerequisiteknowledge: 能独立运行、修改和解释自己的 AI 项目，理解 API、工具调用与基本评估。个别工具缺口可按需自学。
highlights: 预算、权限、评估与运行交接

cases.title: Knowledge Access
cases.context: A regulated services team needs a policy assistant for 40 operations staff across two departments. The same question can have different permitted evidence depending on the caller.
cases.request: Reduce time spent finding the current policy without giving staff access to restricted documents or making policy decisions for them.
constraints: A$24,000 implementation ceiling; A$1,200 monthly operating ceiling.
Four-week pilot; no new customer-facing endpoint.
Documents have department, version, effective date and owner. Identity comes from the server session, never a user prompt.
Answers require accessible current evidence. Conflicting or missing evidence must be escalated.

stakeholders.position: Wants shorter handling time and evidence staff can verify.
Requires denial tests and removal of cross-department access.
Approves only the bounded pilot, not a company-wide rollout.

cases.change: The archive connector is not approved. Keep it out of the pilot and revise coverage, cost and acceptance claims.

records.text: A supervisor must approve exceptions above A$500.
Finance reserves must not be disclosed outside finance.
A supervisor must approve exceptions above A$300.

reference: Choose permission-filtered retrieval with version checks, cited passages and escalation; exclude autonomous policy decisions.
Use an initial two-department access matrix and a curated set of answerable, unanswerable, stale, conflicting and injected requests.
At 4,000 requests, 80% accepted coverage and 6 minutes saved per accepted answer, gross time value is 320 hours or A$19,200 monthly. This is capacity value, not cash saving.
For 4,000 requests at an assumed A$0.04 model cost, plus A$300 infrastructure and 10 maintenance hours at A$60, operating cost is A$1,060. Verify the price assumptions before a live purchase.
An incremental pilot must measure accepted coverage, review minutes, denied access and evidence correctness against the same baseline; do not infer success from these planning numbers.

cases.title: Service Operations
cases.context: A maintenance coordinator receives service requests through email and a CRM webhook. A webhook can be delivered more than once. Calendar and CRM updates may succeed independently.
cases.request: Prepare a service recommendation and an approval-ready appointment draft, keeping the coordinator responsible for committing a visit.
constraints: A$18,000 implementation ceiling; A$700 monthly operating ceiling.
CRM returns requestId and revision; calendar supports idempotency keys.
No appointment may be created before approval of the exact site, time window and revision.
A timeout does not prove that a downstream write failed. Reconcile before retrying.

stakeholders.position: Needs reliable handover and fewer missed requests.
Keeps control of commitments and needs to see missing information.
Requires bounded retries, auditable state and recoverable failures.

cases.change: The CRM endpoint is delayed two weeks. Propose a read-only intake pilot and postpone live booking; do not quietly change the success definition.
reference: Use a bounded workflow: ingest → validate → prepare draft → request approval → revalidate revision → commit → reconcile.
Derive the idempotency key from requestId, approved revision and action; a new eventId alone must not authorize another booking.
Approval for revision 1 is stale after revision 2 arrives. Return to review and display the changed field.
Record calendar success even if the CRM write times out. Query the CRM using the operation key before deciding whether to retry.
When the CRM is unavailable, retain intake and draft preparation only; state that booking-cycle savings cannot yet be established.

cases.title: Purchasing Controls
cases.context: A procurement team reviews purchase requests and supplier documents. Finance owns approval limits; operations wants urgent requests handled quickly.
cases.request: Extract a purchase request, check policy and route it for a human decision. Treat supplier attachments as content, never as authorization.
constraints: A$20,000 implementation ceiling; A$900 monthly operating ceiling.
Requests above A$5,000 need finance approval; all external payments remain out of scope.
Unknown supplier, missing currency or missing requester identity requires review.
A policy change must be versioned and applied to pending requests with explicit revalidation.

stakeholders.position: Needs a consistent queue and traceable evidence.
Owns approval policy and cost reporting.
Wants an urgent route without bypassing finance.

cases.change: The sponsor cuts the implementation budget by 30% and lowers the approval threshold to A$3,000. Preserve the control boundary while reducing scope.
reference: Use extraction plus deterministic policy routing; the model may draft fields but must not approve or pay.
PR-01 routes to the normal approver under the A$5,000 rule, PR-02 to finance and PR-03 to supplier review.
After the threshold falls to A$3,000, PR-01 must be revalidated and routed to finance; a prior normal-route decision cannot be replayed.
With the A$14,000 revised build ceiling, retain intake, supplier checks and approval routing. Defer optional supplier analytics and additional connectors.
Acceptance needs the correct route, valid source fields, immutable policy version and no outbound payment action. Urgency changes queue order, not approval authority.

schedule.title: Tech 的 10 周，怎样一步步推进？
schedule.intro: 前两周看导师怎样调查和判断，第 3–4 周带着结构练习，第 5–10 周独立推进完整项目。预算、治理、评估和客户沟通贯穿每轮。

stages.title: Business Fluency for Engineers
stages.activity: 调查企业目标、部门流程、现有系统与决策关系。识别值得做的 AI 场景，判断哪些需求应先拒绝。
stages.output: Discovery Brief、流程图、机会优先级与项目边界。

stages.title: AI Capabilities and Trade-offs
stages.activity: 比较流程改进、代码自动化、RAG 与 Agent。针对数据、权限和模型限制，验证最不确定的一环。
stages.output: 方案比较、架构图、技术验证与验收标准。

stages.title: The Economics of AI
stages.activity: 估算开发、接入、模型、人工复核和维护成本。明确范围、依赖与停止条件，向预算负责人解释投入。
stages.output: 预算表、Scope、里程碑与交付计划。

stages.title: AI in Enterprise Systems
stages.activity: 接手已有数据和接口，处理身份、访问权限、版本与数据质量，让关键业务链路能够接起来。
stages.output: 接入实现、权限边界与数据处理记录。

stages.title: Agents, Tools and Human Control
stages.activity: 让 Agent 在授权范围内调用工具，处理审批、重复事件、失败重试与人工接管。
stages.output: 可运行工作流、审批状态与异常恢复机制。

stages.title: Evaluation and Reliability
stages.activity: 建立覆盖正常与失败情况的 Evals，比较质量、延迟、模型费用和复核成本，用证据修改系统。
stages.output: 评估集、失败分析、成本与延迟报告。

stages.title: Working with Stakeholders
stages.activity: 带着实现和评估向业务、IT、安全与预算负责人做 Pre，回应冲突，争取下一阶段的决定。
stages.output: 客户展示、评审材料与决定记录。

stages.title: Delivering Through Change
stages.activity: 面对预算削减、接口延期或新增需求，重算范围、架构、费用和时间，再修改实现。
stages.output: Change Request、修订方案与更新后的交付计划。

stages.title: From Prototype to Pilot
stages.activity: 确定试点用户、基线、成功标准和监测方式，分析系统是否值得继续投入，安排用户启用。
stages.output: Pilot Plan、效果核对与 Adoption Plan。

stages.title: AI Adoption and Handover
stages.activity: 完成客户验收与最终展示，让接手者能依据资料独立运行关键流程、定位异常并承担维护。
stages.output: 验收材料、Runbook、维护责任与交接包。

automation.title: 30 项工程交付任务，把 AI 应用带进企业
automation.intro: 能把 AI 应用跑起来以后，还要面对企业的旧系统、访问权限、预算和不断变化的要求。下面 30 项任务按六个交付环节展开，在 10 周的多个案例中组合实践，留下方案、实现和验证的证据。

items.goal: 为同一个需求比较规则自动化、RAG 和 Agent，用限制与验证结果解释选择。
items.result: 方案对照与 Architecture Decision Record。

items.title: Model Routing and Cost Control
items.goal: 按任务比较模型的质量、响应时间与费用，设计路由、缓存和费用上限，再验证代价。
items.result: 模型选择表、路由策略与费用估算。

items.title: Retrieval with Evidence
items.goal: 处理文档分块、检索、版本和引用，让回答能追溯依据，资料不足时有明确的处理方式。
items.result: 检索链路、引用检查与不足信息处理。

items.title: Identity-aware Retrieval
items.goal: 让检索遵守用户、部门和租户的访问权限，检查授权过滤是否真的限制了结果。
items.result: 权限检索实现与跨边界访问检查。

items.title: Context and Knowledge Lifecycle
items.goal: 处理长上下文、知识更新、过期资料和删除要求，说明何时重新检索、失效或刷新。
items.result: 上下文策略、更新流程与知识失效规则。

items.title: Working with Legacy APIs
items.goal: 对接已有接口，处理字段不一致、版本变化、限流和错误码，给出可定位的失败信息。
items.result: 接口适配代码、契约检查与错误映射。

items.title: MCP in Enterprise Systems
items.goal: 为业务工具定义清楚的输入输出、身份和权限边界，检查工具暴露是否超出任务需要。
items.result: MCP 工具适配、参数校验与权限说明。

items.title: Events, Idempotency and Duplicates
items.goal: 处理重复消息、回调和乱序事件，避免一个业务请求生成多次写入或执行。
items.result: 事件处理实现、去重记录与重复输入检查。

items.title: Long-running Workflows
items.goal: 把耗时步骤放入可跟踪的任务流程，处理超时、失败队列、重试上限与进度恢复。
items.result: 任务状态、恢复路径与失败处理代码。

items.title: Deployment and Environment Boundaries
items.goal: 把配置、密钥、数据与运行环境分开管理，让同一份代码能够按明确条件启动和验证。
items.result: 部署配置、环境检查与启动说明。

items.title: Bounded Agent Execution
items.goal: 为 Agent 定义可执行步骤、工具范围、时间和费用上限，检查何时继续、暂停或停止。
items.result: Agent 状态机与执行边界检查。

items.title: Approval-aware Tool Use
items.goal: 让关键动作先取得对应审批；审批后条件发生变化时，检查原决定是否仍然有效。
items.result: 审批状态、工具执行检查与条件变更记录。

items.title: Skills for Team Workflows
items.goal: 把已经验证的操作整理成团队能复用的 Skill，管理输入要求、工具权限、版本和失败处理。
items.result: Skill、使用约定与版本检查。

items.title: Human Handover and Resume
items.goal: 在不确定或失败时保存必要状态，把问题交给负责人；确认后从正确步骤继续，避免重做已完成动作。
items.result: 接管记录、检查点与恢复实现。

items.title: Recovery after Partial Failure
items.goal: 面对部分成功、部分失败的操作，先核对已发生什么，再决定补偿、重试或人工处理。
items.result: 核对流程、补偿策略与故障恢复检查。

items.title: Evals and Regression Gates
items.goal: 把正常输入、边界条件和已知失败放进评估集，为修改模型、Prompt 或工具后的回归设定标准。
items.result: 评估集、对比报告与通过条件。

items.title: Prompt Injection and Trust Boundaries
items.goal: 检查来自文档、邮件与工具结果的指令是否越过信任边界，防止业务内容变成系统授权。
items.result: 攻击输入、处理结果与信任边界说明。

items.title: Testing Retrieval and Permissions
items.goal: 核对答案引用、知识版本、拒答和跨用户访问，把检索正确性与授权正确性分开检查。
items.result: 检索与权限评估、失败分类与修订结果。

items.title: Latency and Unit Economics
items.goal: 在不同并发和任务条件下比较延迟、模型费用与人工复核成本，核算一次合格交付的代价。
items.result: 延迟数据、单次成本与优化取舍。

items.title: Observability and Incident Diagnosis
items.goal: 串起一次请求的工具调用、错误、费用与决定，保留定位所需证据，同时控制日志中的敏感信息。
items.result: Trace、告警条件与故障定位记录。

items.title: Technical Reviews with Stakeholders
items.goal: 带着架构、实现与评估向业务、IT、安全和预算负责人展示，回应不同角色的质询。
items.result: 客户展示材料、决定与待处理问题。

items.title: Engineering through Change
items.goal: 面对预算减少、接口延期或新需求，修改范围、技术方案和计划，再用实现验证影响。
items.result: 变更说明、修订代码与预算计划。

items.title: Release Readiness and Rollback
items.goal: 检查上线条件、版本、监测和责任，设计出现问题后如何停止扩大影响、回退或恢复。
items.result: 上线检查表、版本与回退方案。

items.title: From Pilot to Adoption
items.goal: 限定首批使用范围，用基线、运行问题和复核成本判断继续、调整或停止，再安排用户启用。
items.result: 试点结果分析与用户采用计划。

items.title: Handover that Others Can Run
items.goal: 整理运行、维护和故障处理资料，检查另一位参与者能否按资料运行关键流程并定位异常。
items.result: Runbook、维护责任与完整交接包。

weeks.title: 第 1–2 周｜导师示范与跟练

weeks.title: 第 3–4 周｜有结构的案例训练

modules.title: Enterprise Discovery
modules.heading: 先看懂企业，再判断值得解决的问题
modules.text: 导师带着调查企业怎样完成一单业务，讲清部门、收入成本、系统和决策关系。学生还原流程，再接着提问。
modules.outcome: 业务流程图、Stakeholder Map、事实与未知信息清单。

modules.title: Solution Architecture & Commercial Planning
modules.heading: 把方案、范围、预算与交付计划一起讲清楚
modules.text: 沿用带练案例，比较流程改进、代码自动化、RAG 与 Agent。提出范围、完整成本、依赖和停止条件，做第一次方案 Pitch。
modules.outcome: Proposal、方案比较、架构与预算、里程碑。

modules.title: AI Governance & Reliability
modules.heading: 让数据、安全与可靠性成为交付条件
modules.text: 进入第二个案例，学生按调查提纲访谈业务、IT 和安全负责人。核对数据主权、访问权限、审批与责任，修改方案和关键实现。；为第二个案例建立经业务核对的 golden dataset，区分开发与验收数据，检查错误、遗漏、引用和越权，再答辩是否值得试点。
modules.outcome: 数据流与权限图、审批边界、治理记录与技术验证。；Golden dataset、评分依据、失败分析与修订 Proposal。

modules.title: Enterprise Engineering
modules.heading: 在已有系统里完成接入、实现与评估
modules.text: 启动完整项目，减少调查提示。学生决定找谁核实问题，独立提出方案、预算、验收标准和里程碑，争取客户批准。；在已有代码、数据和接口中实现关键链路。处理最小权限、环境边界、重复事件和长任务，用运行证据检查接入。；验证 Agent 的权限、人工接管和失败恢复，核算质量、延迟、模型与复核成本，按失败证据调整实现。
modules.outcome: 完整项目 Proposal、决策记录、预算与验收计划。；可运行核心流程、接口契约、接入和异常处理证据。；评估报告、成本与性能记录、恢复验证。

modules.title: Stakeholder Leadership
modules.heading: 面对冲突与变更，推动新的决定
modules.text: 面对预算削减、接口延期或新增需求，和业务、IT、安全及预算负责人协商，重算范围、架构、费用与时间。
modules.outcome: Change Request、影响分析、修订方案与决定记录。

modules.title: Enterprise Adoption
modules.heading: 让用户会用，让客户能够接手
modules.text: 用基线、成功标准和试点证据判断投入。向用户讲解怎样操作、检查结果、处理异常，并验证回滚和维护责任。；对照最初承诺接受最终验收，接手者按资料独立运行和处理异常。每人解释自己的贡献、取舍与剩余问题。
modules.outcome: 试点结论、操作说明、启用与回滚计划。；最终系统、验收矩阵、Runbook、交接包与答辩。

faqs.a: 可以先了解 Business，它从业务经验出发，包含 AI 自动化实践、方案、预算和跨团队推进。如果你希望进入 Tech，需要先补齐独立开发与调试 AI 应用的能力。MCP、Skills 等个别工具不熟，可以结合官方资源按需补充。

faqs.q: 和 Business 课程、一对一陪跑有什么区别？

cases.title: ANZ · Z-GPT：银行内部知识怎样接给 AI？
cases.text: 内部资料、回答可靠性和人工责任，需要放在同一个交付方案里考虑。
cases.problem: 如果接手一个类似的银行内部助手，怎样确定可接入的资料、身份边界与回答验收要求？
cases.decision: 课堂从范围可控的内部问答切入，核对来源、权限与人工责任，再讨论是否值得扩展。
cases.tradeoff: 比较现成企业工具、检索问答与定制集成。把资料治理、接入、评估和使用培训都计入投入。
cases.change: 训练条件：一个资料库未获安全批准。重新提出试点范围与预算建议，争取客户决定。
cases.output: 身份与检索权限链路、版本过滤、拒答与引用评估，连同单次成本及异常记录。
cases.facts: ANZ 在 2023 年介绍了内部聊天工具 Z-GPT：通过 Microsoft 使用 OpenAI 模型，围绕部分内部数据开展实验，并强调使用者需要审查回答、对最终决定负责。

cases.title: Woolworths · Olive：从问答到购物动作
cases.text: 能推荐商品以后，还要界定哪些动作由助手做、哪些必须由用户确认。
cases.problem: 当助手从回答问题变成添加商品，怎样设计用户控制、商品数据和工具执行之间的边界？
cases.decision: 课堂把建议、加入购物篮和结账分开。商品信息以业务系统为准；修改购物篮可撤回，结账由用户完成。
cases.tradeoff: 先验证一段完整的购物流程，再讨论个性化。分别估算商品接入、工具执行、评估和人工支持成本。
cases.change: 训练条件：价格或库存接口不稳定。决定哪些功能应降级、暂停，哪些仍能保留。
cases.output: 商品查询与购物篮工具、用户控制、重复执行防护，以及价格、库存和失败场景的评估。
cases.facts: Woolworths 的 Olive 官方页面介绍了餐食灵感、购物篮建议和添加商品功能；最终结账由用户完成。购物助手与客服助手分开，完整历史订单访问仍未开放。

cases.title: IAG · CASI：理赔团队怎样用 AI 查保单？
cases.text: 找到保单段落只是开始，还要让员工能够核对依据、理解适用范围。
cases.problem: 如果为类似的理赔团队设计保单助手，怎样让员工核对条款、版本与适用条件，而不是直接相信一段回答？
cases.decision: 课堂围绕有引用的保单问答设计流程，区分资料检索、条款解释与最终理赔决定。
cases.tradeoff: 优先支持范围明确的产品与保单版本。把回答复核和资料更新成本纳入价值判断。
cases.change: 训练条件：新旧保单版本同时存在且答案冲突。调整检索、审核和交接安排，再说明扩大试点的条件。
cases.output: 保单版本与适用范围过滤、带来源的回答、冲突与拒答处理，以及按问题类型划分的评估。
cases.facts: IAG 在 2024 年年报中介绍 CASI，用于帮助员工查找保单文件、判断相关保障内容，提高服务效率。

stages.title: Business Fluency for Engineers
stages.activity: 调查企业目标、部门流程、现有系统与决策关系。识别值得做的 AI 场景，判断哪些需求应先拒绝。

stages.title: AI Capabilities and Trade-offs
stages.activity: 比较流程改进、代码自动化、RAG 与 Agent。针对数据、权限和模型限制，验证最不确定的一环。
stages.output: 方案比较、架构图、技术验证与验收标准。

stages.title: The Economics of AI
stages.activity: 估算开发、接入、模型、人工复核和维护成本。明确范围、依赖与停止条件，向预算负责人解释投入。
stages.output: 预算表、Scope、里程碑与交付计划。

stages.title: AI in Enterprise Systems
stages.activity: 接手已有数据和接口，处理身份、访问权限、版本与数据质量，让关键业务链路能够接起来。
stages.output: 接入实现、权限边界与数据处理记录。

stages.title: Agents, Tools and Human Control
stages.activity: 让 Agent 在授权范围内调用工具，处理审批、重复事件、失败重试与人工接管。
stages.output: 可运行工作流、审批状态与异常恢复机制。

stages.title: Evaluation and Reliability
stages.activity: 建立覆盖正常与失败情况的 Evals，比较质量、延迟、模型费用和复核成本，用证据修改系统。
stages.output: 评估集、失败分析、成本与延迟报告。

stages.title: Working with Stakeholders
stages.activity: 带着实现和评估向业务、IT、安全与预算负责人做 Pre，回应冲突，争取下一阶段的决定。
stages.output: 客户展示、评审材料与决定记录。

stages.title: Delivering Through Change
stages.activity: 面对预算削减、接口延期或新增需求，重算范围、架构、费用和时间，再修改实现。
stages.output: Change Request、修订方案与更新后的交付计划。

stages.title: From Prototype to Pilot
stages.activity: 确定试点用户、基线、成功标准和监测方式，分析系统是否值得继续投入，安排用户启用。
stages.output: Pilot Plan、效果核对与 Adoption Plan。

stages.title: AI Adoption and Handover
stages.activity: 完成客户验收与最终展示，让接手者能依据资料独立运行关键流程、定位异常并承担维护。
stages.output: 验收材料、Runbook、维护责任与交接包。

sections.title: 01 · Decision & Client Context
paragraphs: 为 40 位员工建设政策问答助手，覆盖运营、财务与历史资料。建议批准 A$14,880 开发预算，四周上线内部试点。
运营希望减少查找资料的时间，财务关心节省成本，IT 协助接入。试点后根据使用情况扩大。

sections.title: 02 · Discovery & Working Assumptions
paragraphs: 每月 4,000 次查询，每次 8 分钟。预计 AI 覆盖 80%，员工每次复核 2 分钟。
收集部门文档并访谈负责人，开发时调整查询范围。暂按给定数字测算收益，尚未明确如何统计拒绝和失败请求。

sections.title: 03 · Options & Recommendation
paragraphs: 使用 RAG 读取政策并回答问题。相比普通搜索，员工不用逐条打开文档；与自主 Agent 相比，实现范围更集中。
通过提示词要求模型遵守部门权限并引用来源，暂不增加业务动作工具。

sections.title: 04 · Scope & Change Decision
paragraphs: 接入运营、财务及历史档案，尽量提高覆盖率。对接旧系统可能需要额外适配。
历史档案接口尚未获批，但仍放在计划范围里；等待客户确认后继续处理。暂未调整覆盖率目标和交付计划。

sections.title: 05 · Architecture & Access Control
paragraphs: 员工在界面输入问题和部门，后端检索文档，模型整理答案并提供引用，员工确认后使用。
提示词要求不要返回其他部门资料，并优先使用新版本文档。回答日志用于排查问题，后续补充访问与缓存细节。

sections.title: 06 · Budget & Delivery Plan
paragraphs: 调查 24 小时 A$2,880；适配器、检索与界面 80 小时 A$9,600；准备金 A$2,400。总计 A$14,880。
按 A$120/小时估算，计划调查后开发，再邀请员工使用。验收和交接未独立估时，也未列出身份接口、权限审批延误时由谁作决定。

sections.title: 07 · Operating Cost & Business Value
paragraphs: 80% 查询每次减少 6 分钟，每月节省 320 小时。按 A$60/小时，预计每月节约现金 A$19,200。
模型请求 A$160，基础设施 A$300，预计运行费 A$460。此处尚未计入维护、异常处理，也未区分可释放工时与现金支出减少。

sections.title: 08 · Evaluation & Acceptance
paragraphs: 收集常见问题，由运营负责人检查回答。准确率达到 80% 后进入用户试用。
保留错误答案并修正。暂未独立列出跨部门访问、过期政策、注入指令和越权批准的阻断规则。

sections.title: 09 · Pilot & Investment Decision
paragraphs: 内部用户试用四周，记录使用次数、回答反馈与满意度，然后讨论是否推广。
目前没有冻结对比基线；使用量增加是否代表节省时间、出现什么问题必须停止，都需要进一步明确。

sections.title: 10 · Handover & Ownership
paragraphs: 交付代码仓库、README 和配置说明，由 IT 接手。运营继续收集员工反馈。
文档更新、权限事故、缓存失效与回滚流程暂未指定负责人，也没有安排接收方按材料独立运行验证。

sections.title: 01 · Decision & Client Context
paragraphs: 建议批准四周、两个部门的内部试点：帮助 40 位运营与财务员工找到自己有权查看的现行政策，并保留出处。系统不替主管批准例外，也不开放给外部客户。
申请开发预算 A$21,600，低于 A$24,000 上限；预计月运行成本 A$1,060，低于 A$1,200 上限。这里申请的是有边界的试点，不是全公司推广。
运营负责人确认问题与基线；IT 负责人确认接入方式；安全负责人批准权限矩阵；财务负责人决定是否投入。任一必要条件未获确认，不直接进入用户试用。

sections.title: 02 · Discovery & Working Assumptions
paragraphs: 课程任务给定每月 4,000 次查询、原流程每次 8 分钟、人工完全成本每小时 A$60。先访谈两个部门，抽取同类查询，记录找资料、判断版本、请人确认分别花了多久。
80% 可接受覆盖率和每次 2 分钟复核是测算目标，尚不是试点结果。必须记录哪些查询有答案、哪些被拒绝或转交人工，不能只统计回答成功的部分。
启动前需确认现行文档清单、文档负责人、访问组、员工身份接口及撤权机制。不能确认权限或有效版本的资料，不进入检索范围。

sections.title: 03 · Options & Recommendation
paragraphs: 先比较三条路：改进站内搜索、带权限的 RAG、能自主执行业务动作的 Agent。搜索改进便宜，但跨文档回答和引用仍需人工整理；自主 Agent 增加审批与执行风险，本次没有相应业务需求。
选择带权限的检索与引用回答。先用小范围文档验证能否稳定找到现行证据；若普通搜索已满足目标，就不继续增加模型环节。
模型负责组织有依据的答案，服务端负责身份、权限和允许的动作。提示词不能替代访问控制。

sections.title: 04 · Scope & Change Decision
paragraphs: 纳入已批准的运营与财务现行文档；每份资料保留部门、版本、生效日期和负责人。排除外部客户入口、自动批准例外、付款、全公司推广。
客户未批准 archive connector。本版明确移除历史档案接入，不以公开接口或人工复制绕过审批；相关查询覆盖率需重新测量，不能继续沿用原覆盖假设。
若档案接入后续获批，另列工作量、权限测试、运行成本及验收变化，由预算负责人确认后才加入。

sections.title: 05 · Architecture & Access Control
paragraphs: 员工入口 → 服务端会话身份与部门 → 权限及有效版本过滤 → 检索现行证据 → 带引用回答或转交人工 → 员工复核与审计记录。不得先把所有部门文档送进模型，再要求模型保密。
适配器使用独立最小权限凭证；检索与缓存都按授权范围隔离。部门信息来自已认证会话，不接受用户在问题里声明自己的部门。失去权限后重新检查授权，不能继续返回此前缓存的受限内容。
回答保留证据 ID 与版本。POL-01 的现行 v3 优先于已过期 v2；运营员工请求财务 POL-02 时不返回受限证据。来源冲突、缺失或过期时转交负责人。
接口返回 status、evidenceIds、policyVersion、allowedNextAction；有证据时 allowedNextAction 为 staff-review，commitment 为 null。没有证据时返回待人工处理状态，不编造批准结果。

sections.title: 06 · Budget & Delivery Plan
paragraphs: 按 A$120/小时估算，160 小时工程工作合计 A$19,200，另留 A$2,400 风险准备金，总计 A$21,600。费率和工作量是本提案的规划假设，采购前需要核对。
顺序是调查与基线 → 适配器及检索验证 → 权限与质量验收 → 用户试点及交接。四周指客户试点窗口；工程实施结束并通过准入检查后才进入，不把全部开发工时硬塞进四周。
运营提供文档与基线，IT 提供身份及接入，安全批准访问矩阵。接口延期则调整范围与日期；超出准备金的接入工作须重新估价并获得决定。

sections.title: 07 · Operating Cost & Business Value
paragraphs: 每月成本按 4,000 次请求 × A$0.04 = A$160，加基础设施 A$300、维护 10 小时 × A$60 = A$600，合计 A$1,060。单次请求成本须用实际模型、输入长度及重试量重新验证，不把估算当成供应商报价。
若覆盖率达到 80%，每次可接受回答从 8 分钟减少到 2 分钟，每月释放 320 小时，对应 A$19,200 的产能价值。这不是已经实现的现金节省，也不能据此承诺减少岗位。
覆盖率仅 50% 时释放 200 小时，对应 A$12,000；达到 90% 时为 360 小时、A$21,600。试点同时测量复核时间、维护投入和异常处理，判断释放的时间能否真正用于其他工作。

sections.title: 08 · Evaluation & Acceptance
paragraphs: 冻结有代表性的评估集，记录输入、员工身份、文档版本、预期行为和观察结果。将可回答、缺证据、旧版本、来源冲突、跨部门请求及注入内容分别统计。
权限泄漏或越权执行业务动作属于阻断问题；不能用总体回答分数抵消。现行证据引用、拒绝路径与异常转交均需逐项通过；覆盖率和复核时间另行与目标比较。
运营判断答案是否可用；安全核对拒绝与访问边界；IT 核对日志及恢复路径。未通过关键控制前不邀请试点用户。
rows: 返回 POL-01 v3 与出处，交员工复核
运营身份请求财务资料
不返回 POL-02 受限证据
不使用旧阈值，转交负责人
交主管决定，不执行批准
不授予工具权限，不发送资料

sections.title: 09 · Pilot & Investment Decision
paragraphs: 试点第 1 周确认基线、权限矩阵和评估集；第 2 周与客户负责人检查检索、拒绝及缺证据路径；关键问题解决后，第 3 周由约定用户组使用；第 4 周汇总证据并评审。
用同类工作量、同一统计口径比较覆盖率、复核时间、出处问题、支持请求及维护成本。80% 覆盖率仍是目标，最终以记录为准。
质量、成本与维护能力均可接受，才申请扩大；覆盖不足则缩小场景或修改方案；出现权限问题先停止受影响入口。财务、运营、安全与 IT 各自给出继续、修改或停止的依据。

sections.title: 10 · Handover & Ownership
paragraphs: 交付代码版本、文档版本清单、访问矩阵、评估集与结果、配置步骤、运行手册和未解决事项。密钥不写进文档；接收方通过既有凭证管理方式配置。
IT 接收运行与回滚；安全负责人处理访问事件；各部门资料负责人维护文档。新增资料先核对所有者、生效日期和部门，清理旧缓存后重跑引用及拒绝测试。
访问事件发生时先关闭受影响检索入口，保留必要审计线索，通知安全负责人；重查权限矩阵后才能恢复。回滚需同时对应代码与文档快照。
由另一位工程师按交接材料启动项目、运行验收、定位一次被拒绝的请求并说明恢复方式。完成这些检查后，客户才有依据接受交接；试点证据不足的部分继续列为未决事项。

reviews.title: 范围会跟着客户决定改变
reviews.before: 历史档案尚未获批，初稿仍把它算进覆盖范围。
reviews.question: 接口未获批准，凭什么把相关能力写进交付范围？
reviews.after: 移除 archive connector，重新测量覆盖率；获批后再评估费用与验收。

reviews.title: 权限不能交给提示词
reviews.before: 用户自行填写部门，模型被要求替系统保密。
reviews.question: 如果运营员工把部门填成财务，会发生什么？
reviews.after: 从服务端会话取身份，在检索前过滤权限，并检查撤权与缓存。

reviews.title: 能写代码，还得算完整交付
reviews.before: A$14,880 只覆盖调查、开发与准备金。
reviews.question: 测试、试点准备和交接由谁做，需要多少工时？
reviews.after: 补入 32h 验证与 24h 交接，总预算 A$21,600，仍在上限内。

reviews.title: 收益要能经得起财务追问
reviews.before: 把 A$19,200 产能价值写成现金节省，运行费漏算维护。
reviews.question: 工资没有减少，这笔钱真的省下来了吗？
reviews.after: 区分产能与现金；列覆盖率敏感性，运行费补至 A$1,060/月。

reviews.title: 平均分不能掩盖关键错误
reviews.before: 只要求回答准确率达到 80%。
reviews.question: 如果答案总体不错，却泄露了一份财务政策，能上线吗？
reviews.after: 将权限泄漏、越权执行设为阻断条件，分别检查引用、拒绝与升级。

reviews.title: 交仓库不等于客户接得住
reviews.before: 交代码与 README，默认 IT 能维护。
reviews.question: 资料更新或权限出事后，谁处理、怎么恢复？
reviews.after: 补齐责任人、文档版本、回滚和事件处理；由接收方独立运行检查。

proposalShowcase.reviewIntro: 先评方案，再看实现，最后看客户能否接手。你要向导师和同学讲自己的判断；同学从业务、IT、安全和预算负责人的角度追问。评审会回到你的方案和工程证据，而不只看展示是否流畅。

reviewSteps.title: 方案阶段 · Proposal Review
reviewSteps.text: 带着 Discovery Brief、架构、范围和预算做 Pre。导师追问问题是否值得做、方案为何这样选，以及哪些条件还没有确认。

reviewSteps.title: 工程阶段 · Technical Review
reviewSteps.text: 打开关键实现，拿权限检查、失败记录和 Evals 支持你的判断。方案里答应的事，要能在系统行为中找到证据。

reviewSteps.title: 变更之后 · Client Pitch
reviewSteps.text: 对照评审意见修改方案和实现，解释范围、费用与风险的变化，再讲清希望客户批准什么、接下来由谁负责。

proposalShowcase.decision: 修订版决定：先做有权限边界的内部试点，开发 A$21,600，预计运行 A$1,060/月。

capabilities.title: 十个维度，练出完整的 FDE 交付能力
capabilities.intro: 看你能否解释决定、拿出证据，并在条件变化后调整。评审关注每个人的材料、现场表现和实际贡献。

items.title: Business Acumen
items.text: 理解企业如何创造收入、承担成本，判断问题是否值得投入。

items.title: Client Discovery
items.text: 主动调查陌生业务，核实假设、基线、决策权和项目边界。

items.title: Solution Architecture
items.text: 比较技术路线，根据客户限制解释架构和取舍。

items.title: Commercial Planning
items.text: 确定范围、完整预算、里程碑、依赖和停止条件。

items.title: AI Governance
items.text: 把数据主权、权限、安全、审批和责任落实为控制。

items.title: Engineering Execution
items.text: 在已有系统中实现接入，处理重复事件、重试和故障恢复。

items.title: AI Reliability
items.text: 建立 golden dataset 和验收标准，用评估证据检查质量、成本与延迟。

items.title: Stakeholder Leadership
items.text: 协调业务、IT、安全和预算负责人，在冲突与变化中推动决定。

items.title: Executive Communication
items.text: 面向决策者讲清投入、风险和收益依据，回应质疑并争取批准。

items.title: Enterprise Adoption
items.text: 推动用户采用，完成培训、试点判断、独立接手和运行维护。

schedule.title: How the 10-week Tech course progresses
schedule.intro: Observe and participate in weeks 1–2, practise with a guide in weeks 3–4, then own the main project in weeks 5–10. Budget, governance, evaluation and client decisions recur throughout.

stages.title: Business Fluency for Engineers
stages.activity: Investigate enterprise goals, workflows, systems and decision authority. Qualify opportunities and reject weak use cases.
stages.output: Discovery brief, workflow, priorities and project boundaries.

stages.title: AI Capabilities and Trade-offs
stages.activity: Compare process changes, code automation, RAG and agents. Validate the least certain technical assumption.
stages.output: Options comparison, architecture, technical spike and acceptance criteria.

stages.title: The Economics of AI
stages.activity: Estimate build, integration, model, review and maintenance costs. Define scope, dependencies and stop conditions.
stages.output: Budget, scope, milestones and delivery plan.

stages.title: AI in Enterprise Systems
stages.activity: Work with existing data and APIs, identity, access, versions and data quality.
stages.output: Working integrations, access boundaries and data-processing records.

stages.title: Agents, Tools and Human Control
stages.activity: Control tool access, approvals, duplicates, retries and human takeover.
stages.output: Working agent workflow, approval states and recovery mechanisms.

stages.title: Evaluation and Reliability
stages.activity: Evaluate normal and failure cases across quality, latency, model costs and review effort.
stages.output: Evaluation set, failure analysis, cost and latency findings.

stages.title: Working with Stakeholders
stages.activity: Present implementation and evaluation evidence to business, IT, security and budget owners.
stages.output: Client presentation, review pack and decision log.

stages.title: Delivering Through Change
stages.activity: Recalculate scope, architecture, cost and time after budget cuts, API delays or new requirements.
stages.output: Change request, revised solution and updated delivery plan.

stages.title: From Prototype to Pilot
stages.activity: Define pilot users, baseline, success criteria and monitoring; assess further investment and adoption.
stages.output: Pilot plan, outcome assessment and adoption plan.

stages.title: AI Adoption and Handover
stages.activity: Complete acceptance and demonstrate that another person can operate, troubleshoot and maintain the workflow.
stages.output: Acceptance evidence, runbook, ownership and handover pack.

schedule.note: Confirm cohort dates and session times before enrolment. Any foundation self-study is additional.

automation.title: 30 engineering tasks to take AI applications into the enterprise
automation.intro: Once an AI app works, enterprise delivery adds legacy systems, access restrictions, budgets and changing requirements. These 30 tasks span six delivery areas and combine across multiple cases over 10 weeks, producing proposal, implementation and validation evidence.
automation.roleNote: Combine tasks across multiple customer cases, from discovery and design through implementation, evaluation and handover. When requirements change, revise the code and explain the effects on scope, cost and risk.
automation.closing: Independent AI application development is the entry point. Class time focuses on enterprise engineering delivery; official resources support specific foundational gaps.

categories.label: Discovery & Delivery Planning
categories.description: Understand the customer environment before committing engineering effort.

categories.label: Architecture & Trade-offs
categories.description: Make architecture choices against data, access, quality and cost constraints.

categories.label: Enterprise Integration
categories.description: Connect existing interfaces and data under operational constraints.

categories.label: Agents & Workflow Control
categories.description: Bound tool use and make workflows stoppable, inspectable and recoverable.

categories.label: Evaluation & Reliability
categories.description: Use quality, access, latency and cost evidence to judge delivery readiness.

categories.label: Customer Delivery & Handover
categories.description: Handle change with working evidence, then prepare the pilot and handover.

items.title: Enterprise System Discovery
items.goal: Inspect an unfamiliar repository, interface documentation and operating records to trace a business request and identify gaps.
items.result: System boundary map, interface inventory and investigation questions.

items.title: Discovery under Uncertainty
items.goal: Investigate incomplete customer requirements and distinguish evidence, assumptions and unknowns about users, decision-makers and constraints.
items.result: Discovery brief and explicit assumptions.

items.title: Data Readiness and Ownership
items.goal: Check schemas, missing values, versions, ownership and access conditions to decide what data can enter the first phase.
items.result: Data readiness assessment and ownership boundaries.

items.title: Baselines and Acceptance
items.goal: Turn requests for better accuracy or speed into inspectable requirements, a baseline and an initial set of checks.
items.result: Baseline, acceptance criteria and initial check set.

items.title: Scope, Budget and Delivery
items.goal: Estimate discovery, implementation, integration, model usage, review and maintenance, including dependencies and stopping conditions.
items.result: Scope, budget assumptions and phased delivery plan.

items.title: Choosing the Right Architecture
items.goal: Compare deterministic automation, RAG and agents for the same requirement, using constraints and validation evidence.
items.result: Architecture comparison and decision record.

items.title: Model Routing and Cost Control
items.goal: Compare models by task quality, response time and cost, then validate routing, caching and spending limits.
items.result: Model comparison, routing strategy and cost estimate.

items.title: Retrieval with Evidence
items.goal: Build retrieval with chunking, versions and citations, including explicit handling of insufficient evidence.
items.result: Retrieval implementation, citation checks and insufficient-evidence handling.

items.title: Identity-aware Retrieval
items.goal: Enforce user, department and tenant access in retrieval and check whether authorisation actually constrains results.
items.result: Authorised retrieval and boundary-access checks.

items.title: Context and Knowledge Lifecycle
items.goal: Handle long context, updates, stale sources and removal requirements with clear retrieval and invalidation decisions.
items.result: Context strategy, update flow and knowledge lifecycle rules.

items.title: Working with Legacy APIs
items.goal: Adapt existing APIs with inconsistent fields, versions, rate limits and error responses.
items.result: API adapter, contract checks and error mapping.

items.title: MCP in Enterprise Systems
items.goal: Define tool inputs, outputs, identity and access boundaries, checking exposure against the actual business need.
items.result: MCP adapter, parameter validation and access contract.

items.title: Events, Idempotency and Duplicates
items.goal: Handle repeated messages, callbacks and out-of-order events without duplicating business writes or actions.
items.result: Event handler, deduplication record and repeat-input checks.

items.title: Long-running Workflows
items.goal: Track long-running work through timeouts, failed-job queues, bounded retries and recovery.
items.result: Job state, recovery paths and failure-handling code.

items.title: Deployment and Environment Boundaries
items.goal: Separate configuration, secrets, data and runtime environments so the same code starts under explicit, verifiable conditions.
items.result: Deployment configuration, environment checks and startup instructions.

items.title: Bounded Agent Execution
items.goal: Define steps, tools, time and cost limits, and verify when an agent continues, pauses or stops.
items.result: Agent state machine and execution-boundary checks.

items.title: Approval-aware Tool Use
items.goal: Require approval for consequential actions and check whether it remains valid when conditions change.
items.result: Approval state, execution checks and changed-condition records.

items.title: Skills for Team Workflows
items.goal: Package validated operations as reusable skills with input requirements, tool access, versioning and failure handling.
items.result: Reusable skill, usage contract and version checks.

items.title: Human Handover and Resume
items.goal: Preserve state for human decisions, then resume from the correct step without repeating completed actions.
items.result: Handover record, checkpoints and resume implementation.

items.title: Recovery after Partial Failure
items.goal: Reconcile partially completed actions before choosing compensation, retry or human intervention.
items.result: Reconciliation flow, compensation strategy and recovery checks.

items.title: Evals and Regression Gates
items.goal: Build evaluations from normal inputs, boundaries and known failures, with regression criteria for model, prompt and tool changes.
items.result: Evaluation set, comparison report and regression criteria.

items.title: Prompt Injection and Trust Boundaries
items.goal: Check whether instructions from documents, email and tool results cross trust boundaries or are mistaken for authority.
items.result: Adversarial inputs, observed outcomes and trust-boundary analysis.

items.title: Testing Retrieval and Permissions
items.goal: Evaluate citations, knowledge versions, abstention and cross-user access as distinct retrieval and authorisation concerns.
items.result: Retrieval and permission evaluation with failure analysis.

items.title: Latency and Unit Economics
items.goal: Compare latency, model spend and human review across workloads, estimating cost per accepted outcome.
items.result: Latency measurements, unit-cost analysis and optimisation trade-offs.

items.title: Observability and Incident Diagnosis
items.goal: Trace tools, errors, costs and decisions across a request, retaining useful evidence while controlling sensitive log content.
items.result: Traces, alert conditions and incident diagnosis records.

items.title: Technical Reviews with Stakeholders
items.goal: Review architecture, implementation and evaluations with business, IT, security and budget stakeholders.
items.result: Customer presentation, decision record and open issues.

items.title: Engineering through Change
items.goal: Respond to budget cuts, delayed interfaces or new requirements by revising scope, architecture and implementation.
items.result: Change record, revised code and updated budget and plan.

items.title: Release Readiness and Rollback
items.goal: Check release conditions, versions, monitoring and ownership, and plan containment, rollback and recovery.

faqs.q: Can I join without taking JR Academy’s AI Engineer course?
faqs.a: Yes. Tech requires the ability to build, debug and explain your own AI applications; purchasing JR Academy AI Engineer first is not required. The two FDE courses also have separate enrolment.

faqs.q: I know the business but cannot build AI applications independently. Which course fits?
faqs.a: Explore Business first: it builds on domain experience with AI automation, proposals, budgets and cross-team delivery. Tech requires independent AI application development and debugging. Specific gaps in MCP, Skills or other tools can be addressed with official resources.

faqs.q: How much time should I set aside?
faqs.a: The current design is 10 weeks, with a 3-hour weekly workshop and around 3–5 hours of project and presentation preparation. Confirm actual cohort dates and session times before enrolment.

faqs.q: How does this differ from Business training and one-to-one coaching?
faqs.a: Tech requires independent AI implementation. Business is a separate course focused on business judgment, proposals, budgets and adoption. They have separate enrolment. One-to-one coaching addresses an individual background and project.

faqs.q: What role do the official Claude courses play?
faqs.a: Use official resources to fill specific gaps in models, APIs, Claude Code, MCP and Skills before class, and consult their pilot and adoption methods during cases. JR Academy organises the main workshops around solution design, implementation, evaluation and customer delivery.

faqs.q: Are the salary targets guaranteed outcomes?
faqs.a: No. A$200,000+ in Australia and US$250,000+ in North America describe career targets. Outcomes depend on experience, skills, interviews and market conditions. The course does not guarantee employment or salary.

proposalShowcase.title: A proposal must stand up to scrutiny
proposalShowcase.intro: Start with a client brief, propose a solution, present it, answer questions and revise the plan. Read both complete versions of the Knowledge Access course case below.
proposalShowcase.summary: 40 staff across two departments need faster access to current policy, within their existing permissions, budget and approval boundaries.
proposalShowcase.readerIntro: Both complete versions are available below. The revised proposal contains the recommendation; the first draft preserves unresolved decisions so you can follow the reasoning behind each change.

sections.title: 01 · Decision & Client Context
paragraphs: Build an internal policy assistant for 40 staff, including operations, finance and archive documents. Request A$14,880 and launch an internal pilot in four weeks.
Operations wants faster lookup, finance wants savings and IT supports integration. Expand after reviewing usage.

sections.title: 02 · Discovery & Working Assumptions
paragraphs: Assume 4,000 monthly requests, eight minutes per manual lookup, 80% AI coverage and two minutes of review.
Collect departmental documents and interview owners, refining scope during implementation. The draft does not yet define how rejected and failed requests enter the coverage calculation.

sections.title: 03 · Options & Recommendation
paragraphs: Use RAG to read policy and answer questions with citations. Compared with search, staff need not open every result; compared with an autonomous agent, the implementation is narrower.
Instruct the model to respect departmental permissions and cite sources. Do not add business-action tools at this stage.

sections.title: 04 · Scope & Change Decision
paragraphs: Include operations, finance and archive documents to maximise coverage. Legacy integration may require additional adaptation.
The archive interface is not yet approved but remains in the delivery scope. Wait for the client’s answer without revising coverage or the plan.

sections.title: 05 · Architecture & Access Control
paragraphs: Staff enter a question and department. The backend retrieves documents, the model summarises an answer with citations and staff check it before use.
Ask the model not to reveal other departments’ documents and to prefer current versions. Keep answer logs; detailed authorisation and cache behaviour remain unresolved.

sections.title: 06 · Budget & Delivery Plan
paragraphs: Estimate 24 discovery hours at A$2,880, 80 adapter/retrieval/UI hours at A$9,600 and A$2,400 contingency: A$14,880 total.
Assume A$120/hour. Discover, build and invite users. Acceptance and handover have no separate effort allowance; identity-interface and permission-approval delays have no assigned decision owner.

sections.title: 07 · Operating Cost & Business Value
paragraphs: At 80% coverage and six minutes released per accepted request, estimate 320 hours and A$19,200 monthly cash savings.

Estimate A$160 model requests plus A$300 infrastructure, totalling A$460/month. Maintenance and exception handling are not included; released capacity has not been distinguished from reduced cash expenditure.

sections.title: 08 · Evaluation & Acceptance
paragraphs: Collect common questions and ask operations to assess answers. Begin user trials once answer accuracy reaches 80%.
Retain and correct wrong answers. The draft has no separate blocking rules for cross-department access, outdated policy, injected instructions or unauthorised approval.

sections.title: 09 · Pilot & Investment Decision
paragraphs: Run a four-week internal trial, recording usage, feedback and satisfaction before considering rollout.
There is no frozen comparative baseline. The draft does not establish whether increased usage means time saved or which incidents require a stop.

sections.title: 10 · Handover & Ownership
paragraphs: Deliver the repository, README and configuration notes for IT to take over. Operations continues collecting feedback.
Ownership of source updates, access incidents, cache invalidation and rollback is unresolved. No receiver-run acceptance check has been specified.

sections.title: 01 · Decision & Client Context
paragraphs: Approve a four-week internal pilot for two departments, helping 40 operations and finance staff find current policy they are authorised to read. Answers retain their sources. The system does not approve policy exceptions or serve external customers.
Request A$21,600 for the build against a A$24,000 ceiling, with estimated monthly running costs of A$1,060 against a A$1,200 ceiling. This decision covers a bounded pilot, not a company-wide rollout.
Operations confirms the problem and baseline; IT confirms integration; security approves the access matrix; finance approves investment. Missing approval blocks user access.

sections.title: 02 · Discovery & Working Assumptions
paragraphs: The course brief supplies 4,000 monthly requests, eight minutes per manual lookup and an assumed loaded labour cost of A$60/hour. Interview both departments and measure time spent finding information, checking versions and obtaining confirmation on comparable requests.
Accepted coverage of 80% and two minutes of review per accepted answer are planning targets, not measured results. Count unanswered, rejected and escalated requests as well as successful answers.

Before starting, confirm approved documents, owners, access groups, the staff identity interface and revocation behaviour. Exclude documents without a confirmed permission boundary or effective version.

sections.title: 03 · Options & Recommendation
paragraphs: Compare improved keyword search, permission-filtered RAG and an autonomous action-taking agent. Search is cheaper but leaves cross-document synthesis and citations to staff. Autonomous execution adds approval risk without an established need in this brief.
Recommend permission-filtered retrieval with cited answers. First validate retrieval against a small approved document set. If ordinary search meets the objective, do not add a model unnecessarily.
The model organises supported answers. The server owns identity, permissions and allowed actions; prompts do not replace access control.

sections.title: 04 · Scope & Change Decision
paragraphs: Include approved current operations and finance documents, retaining department, version, effective date and owner. Exclude customer-facing access, autonomous exception approval, payments and company-wide rollout.

The client has not approved the archive connector. Remove archive ingestion from this revision rather than bypassing approval by copying data or using another endpoint. Remeasure coverage without the archive.
If approval arrives later, estimate the additional integration effort, access tests, running costs and acceptance changes. Obtain a budget decision before adding the work.

sections.title: 05 · Architecture & Access Control
paragraphs: Staff interface → server session identity and department → authorised current-document retrieval → cited answer or escalation → staff review and audit trace. Never send every department’s documents to the model and ask it to keep them confidential.

Use a separate least-privilege adapter credential. Partition retrieval and caches by authorisation. Derive department from the authenticated session, not from a user-supplied statement. Recheck permissions after revocation and do not return previously cached restricted content.

Retain evidence IDs and policy versions. Current POL-01 v3 takes precedence over expired v2. Operations users cannot retrieve restricted finance document POL-02. Missing, conflicting or outdated evidence is escalated.

Return status, evidenceIds, policyVersion and allowedNextAction. Evidence-backed responses allow staff-review and set commitment to null. Missing evidence produces a human-review state, never an invented approval.

sections.title: 06 · Budget & Delivery Plan
paragraphs: At an assumed A$120/hour, 160 engineering hours cost A$19,200. Add A$2,400 contingency for a A$21,600 total. Validate the rate and effort before procurement.

Sequence discovery and baseline, adapter and retrieval validation, access and quality acceptance, then user pilot and handover. The four weeks describe the client pilot window after implementation and admission checks, not a promise to complete all engineering within four weeks.

Operations supplies documents and baseline evidence; IT supplies identity and integration; security approves the access matrix. Interface delays require revised scope and dates. Work beyond contingency requires a new estimate and approval.

sections.title: 07 · Operating Cost & Business Value
paragraphs: Monthly planning cost: 4,000 requests × A$0.04 = A$160, plus A$300 infrastructure and ten maintenance hours × A$60 = A$600, totalling A$1,060. Validate request costs against actual model choice, context size and retries before purchase.

At 80% accepted coverage, reducing each accepted lookup from eight to two minutes releases 320 hours per month, equivalent to A$19,200 of capacity value. This is not realised cash saving or a commitment to remove roles.

At 50% coverage, the estimate falls to 200 hours / A$12,000; at 90%, it rises to 360 hours / A$21,600. Measure review time, maintenance and exceptions to establish whether released time can actually be used elsewhere.

sections.title: 08 · Evaluation & Acceptance
paragraphs: Freeze a representative evaluation set recording input, staff identity, document version, expected behaviour and observed result. Separate answerable, missing-evidence, stale-version, conflicting-source, cross-department and injected-content cases.

A permission leak or unauthorised business action blocks acceptance, regardless of the average answer score. Check current citations, refusal paths and escalation separately. Compare coverage and review time with the planning targets.
Operations judges usability; security checks access denials; IT checks traceability and recovery. Critical controls must pass before inviting users.

sections.title: 09 · Pilot & Investment Decision
paragraphs: Pilot week 1 confirms the baseline, access matrix and evaluation set. Week 2 checks retrieval, denials and missing-evidence paths with the client owners. Once critical issues are resolved, the agreed users begin in week 3. Week 4 consolidates evidence and reviews the investment decision.
Compare accepted coverage, review time, source issues, support requests and maintenance using the same workload and denominator. Coverage of 80% remains a target until supported by records.

Request expansion only if quality, cost and maintainability are acceptable. Narrow or revise the solution if coverage is insufficient. Disable an affected route following an access incident. Finance, operations, security and IT provide their respective reasons to continue, revise or stop.

sections.title: 10 · Handover & Ownership
paragraphs: Deliver the code revision, document-version inventory, access matrix, evaluation set and results, configuration steps, runbook and open issues. Keep secrets out of documents; the receiver uses the existing credential-management process.

IT owns operation and rollback; security owns access incidents; departmental document owners maintain sources. Validate ownership, effective date and department before adding a document. Invalidate stale caches and rerun citation and denial checks.

For an access incident, disable the affected retrieval route, retain the necessary audit trace and notify security. Recheck the access matrix before reopening. Rollback must match both code and document snapshots.

Another engineer uses the handover material to start the project, run acceptance checks, locate a denied request and explain recovery. The client can then judge handover readiness. Unsupported pilot claims remain open issues.
